ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is brown with a dark lateral band and cream-colored throat. Males exhibit characteristic foot-flagging behavior and possess a prominent, elongated third finger.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Nelliyampathi Dancing Frog is best distinguished by the distinct, bright yellow-orange patch on its throat, which contrasts sharply with its otherwise brownish body.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus nelliyampathi* inhabits rocky, fast-flowing streams within evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nelliyampathi dancing frog performs rhythmic "foot-flagging" displays, extending and waving its hind legs to communicate with rivals and mates near fast-flowing streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus nelliyampathi* breeds during the monsoon, laying eggs in stream-bed crevices. Females deposit small clutches of unpigmented eggs hidden beneath gravel.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Nelliyampathi dancing frog is endemic to the Nelliyampathi Hills in the southern Western Ghats of Kerala, India, typically found at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Nelliyampathi Dancing Frog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic chirps, typically heard near fast-flowing rocky streams in its forest habitat.
